The new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro chips debuted this week, but we've since learned about three things Apple didn't highlight.

#1: Memory bandwidth varies across configurations

If you're planning to order a Mac mini, the ordering page doesn't fully detail one key spec: memory bandwidth. Checking the tech specs reveals that your RAM choice may directly affect overall memory bandwidth.

The base M6 Mac mini with 16GB of RAM offers 153GB/s memory bandwidth. But if you upgrade to 24GB or 32GB of RAM, that number jumps to 170GB/s.

Additionally, you'll need to opt for the M5 Pro to get the top memory bandwidth of 307GB/s.

Each configuration is still an improvement over the M4 model, but the differences are worth noting.

#2: N1 chip brings Thread support

When Apple announced the new Mac mini, it highlighted support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, both upgrades over the M4 model's Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3.

But checking the tech specs reveals that the M6 Mac mini includes Apple's own N1 chip. As a result, the Mac mini also supports Thread.

Thread has been built into iPhones since the iPhone 15 Pro, with Apple touting its benefits for smart home accessories and automation. But this is a first for the Mac mini.

#3: Ships with macOS Golden Gate

If you're planning to hold off on installing a new version of macOS for now, you'll want to know that the M6 Mac mini comes preloaded with macOS Golden Gate.

Apple didn't explicitly mention this on its website. However, the company reportedly confirmed to John Gruber that the new version of macOS is preinstalled.

This isn't too surprising since the M6 Mac mini doesn't ship until September 22. macOS 27 will likely launch the week prior—around September 14. But users with concerns about upgrading to the latest software should take note.

For a complete rundown of everything new with the M6 Mac mini compared to the M4 model, check out our summary.

You can pre-order the M6 and M5 Pro Mac mini starting today, priced from $899.

Are you planning to buy an M6 Mac mini? Let us know why in the comments.
